name: Sony FE 16-35mm F2.8 GM II
famousFor: Sony's second-generation constant-f/2.8 ultra-wide GM zoom, marketed as the world's smallest and lightest autofocus F2.8 16-35mm zoom and praised for near coma-free 16mm astro shots.
strengths: Corner-to-corner sharpness wide open at f/2.8, rivaling prime lenses at some focal lengths
About 20% lighter and more compact than the original GM version
Fast, near-silent autofocus from four XD linear motors, good for stills and video AF
Very close 0.22 m minimum focus distance with 0.32x magnification, unusual for an ultra-wide zoom
weaknesses: Noticeable corner shading (about 3/4 stop) at f/2.8, though it clears up when stopped down
Mild coma stretching at 24-35mm compared to the near-perfect 16mm corners
Manual focus ring feels comparatively loose
bestFor: Milky Way and night-sky astrophotography at 16mm
Landscape and architecture work needing edge-to-edge sharpness
Run-and-gun handheld and gimbal video work
Interiors and environmental portraits in low light

name: Sony FE 24mm F1.4 GM
notes: Launch price of $1,398 is from a press/retailer report; Sony's own Alpha Universe announcement rounds it to "approximately $1,400 US".
famousFor: One of the fastest and lightest 24mm primes for full-frame mirrorless, widely regarded as a benchmark lens for astrophotography and night landscapes thanks to very low coma.
strengths: Uncannily sharp edge-to-edge wide open, earning DPReview's 2018 prime lens of the year
Excellent coma control at f/1.4, a favorite for Milky Way and night-sky shooting
Very light for an f/1.4 24mm (445 g), the lightest in its class at launch
Smooth, round bokeh from an 11-blade aperture with minimal onion-ring artifacts
weaknesses: Visible purple/green fringing wide open at f/1.4 that clears up by f/2-f/2.8
Noticeable vignetting wide open, mostly resolved by f/2.8
Moderate focus breathing when racking focus, relevant for video
bestFor: Wide-aperture landscape and architecture shots with shallow depth of field
Astro-landscape composites requiring sharp, low-coma corners

name: Sony FE 50mm F1.2 GM
notes: Sony's own materials highlight 3 XA elements but do not publish a full breakdown of the remaining 11 elements (e.g. any ED glass), so only the XA count is listed. Launch price is Sony's own "approximately $2,000 USD" figure.
famousFor: Sony's first full-frame f/1.2 prime, notable for reaching that aperture in a body comparable in size and weight to many f/1.4 50mm lenses.
strengths: High resolution corner-to-corner even wide open at f/1.2
Compact and relatively light for an f/1.2 50mm, similar to some f/1.4 competitors
Fast, quiet autofocus from four XD linear motors
Smooth, rounded G Master bokeh from an 11-blade aperture
weaknesses: Noticeable focus breathing when racking focus
Bokeh rendering can look somewhat neutral/clinical rather than characterful to some users
Expensive relative to conventional f/1.4 50mm primes
bestFor: Portraits with very shallow depth of field and creamy background blur
Environmental portraits where subject separation is a priority
